chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Umar ibn Uthman, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Said ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said:

Gabriel descended upon Adam (peace be upon them both) and said: O Adam, I have been commanded to give you the choice of one of three things, so choose one and leave the other two. Adam said to him: And what are the three, O Gabriel? He said: Intellect, modesty, and religion. Adam said: I have chosen intellect. So Gabriel said to modesty and religion: Depart and leave him. They both said: O Gabriel, we have been commanded to be with intellect wherever it goes. He said: As you wish. Then he ascended.

key_terms.الحياء: Modesty, moral shame -- an inner quality that restrains one from indecency and wrongdoing
key_terms.الدين: Religion, faith -- the complete system of belief and practice in Islam
key_terms.العقل: Intellect, reason -- the faculty of rational discernment, considered in Shia tradition as the first creation of God and the foundation of religious obligation

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between intellect, modesty, and religion according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq recounts a dialogue between Gabriel and Adam (peace be upon them) in which Adam was given a choice between intellect, modesty, and religion. When Adam chose intellect, modesty and religion declared they were commanded to always accompany it. The hadith, transmitted through Imam Ali (AS), establishes intellect as the foundational virtue upon which both moral and religious life depend -- a theme central to Shia theological anthropology.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. `Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from his grandfather from `Umar b. `Uthman from Abi Jamila al-Mufaddal b. Salih from Sa`id b. Turayf from al-Asbagh b. Nubata from `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said:

Gabriel (as) descended upon Adam (as) and said: O Adam! I was commanded to give you the choice between one of three things. So, choose one and leave the other two. So, Adam said to him: What are the three, Gabriel? He said: Intellect, modesty, and religion. Adam said: I have chosen intellect. So, Gabriel said to modesty and religion: Go and leave him. They said: O Gabriel! Surely, we were commanded to be with the intellect wherever it goes. He said: As you wish. Then, he ascended.
